1. Model consistently underestimates true prices, especially in the early part of the 30-day horizon — adjust forecast upward by 2–5% for the first 5–7 days.  
2. After a sharp price spike (e.g., >40), model tends to overshoot and then correct — reduce forecast by 1–3% in the next 3–5 days post-spike.  
3. Model exhibits mean reversion bias — if 30-day average of true prices is higher than forecast, increase forecast by 1–3% to align with recent trend.  
4. Model lags behind true price movements by 1–3 days — shift forecast forward by 1–2 days for the first 5–7 days of the horizon.  
5. For horizon >15 days, model underestimates the final 5–7 days — increase forecast by 2–4% for the last 5–7 days to capture tail risk.
